alt: Poster: Sensex 81,028.02 (+2.17%), Nifty 50 25,030.35 (+2.01%), Nifty Smallcap 100 about -0.8% on 6 Nov 2026
text:
Indian benchmarks extended their winning run to a seventh session on Friday, with Sensex up over 1,700 points and Nifty back above 25,000, while broader markets lagged.

• Sensex closed at 81,028.02, up 1,718.01 points (2.17%); Nifty 50 closed at 25,030.35, up 493.75 points (2.01%), per ChiniMandi and HDFC Sky closing reports. Kotak Neo reports the same closing levels.
• The seven-session run is reported by ChiniMandi and HDFC Sky; HDFC Sky describes it as the Nifty's longest in 14 months.
• Nifty Smallcap 100 fell about 0.8% and Nifty Midcap 100 ended marginally lower, per Kotak Neo and HDFC Sky.
• Reports cite crude oil moves and the ongoing West Asia conflict as drivers; ChiniMandi and HDFC Sky both note that the recovery is not yet broad-based.

Our view: index gains led by large private banks alongside weaker mid and smallcaps suggest participation is still selective. A run of this length says little about what comes next, and moves tied to crude and geopolitical headlines can change quickly. This is an interpretation, not a prediction or advice.

For practitioners: when benchmarks rally but mid and smallcaps fall, how do you read the quality of the move?
